# Toy of the Year 1997

## Eh-oh! It's the Teletubbies!

**Tinky Winky, Dipsy, La-la and Po have swept aside all competitors to win the top award in the UK toy industry, the British Association of Toy Retailer’s (BATR) Toy of the Year 1997/1998.**

The award was presented in front of an audience of around 600 from both sides of the toy industry at a gala dinner at the Royal Lancaster Hotel, London on Sunday 1st February 1998.

BATR chairman, David Fogel says, “In an industry dominated by powerful multi-national companies, I am delighted that our award has been won by a family-run British toy company, Golden Bear in Telford, with toys based on a British television programme.”

The originators of the ‘virtual pets’ craze raging around the world, Tamagotchi (Bandai) won most Innovative Toy of the Year, Hasbro’s Action Man Skydiver was Boy’s Toy of the Year, while a Spanish company, Famosa scooped Girl’s Toy of the Year with a doll that can change it’s expression. Star Wars Monopoly (Waddingtons) was voted Game of the Year.

Toy Options, with Buzz Lightyear in 1996 (which continued high sales right through 1997) and Spice Girls dolls which only arrived in December, won Toy Company of the Year award.

**Golden Bear Products Ltd.** is a British toy manufacturing company that was formed in 1979 by John Hales and Christine Nicholls.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Bear_Toys#cite_note-:0-1) Golden Bear operates from its headquarters in [Telford, Shropshire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telford,_Shropshire "Telford, Shropshire")[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Bear_Toys#cite_note-:1-2) and opened an office in [Hong Kong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hong_Kong "Hong Kong") in 2001.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Bear_Toys#cite_note-3)

## Products

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Golden_Bear_Toys&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Products")]

The company has sold a broad range of licensed and branded products including _[Thomas & Friends](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas\_&\_Friends "Thomas & Friends")_, My 1st [JCB](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J._C._Bamford "J. C. Bamford"), _[Charlie and Lola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlie\_and\_Lola "Charlie and Lola")_, _[Pingu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pingu "Pingu")_, _[Noddy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Noddy\_(character) "Noddy (character)")_, _[Peppa Pig](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peppa\_Pig "Peppa Pig")_, _[Brum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brum\_(TV\_series) "Brum (TV series)")_, _[Bob the Builder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob\_the\_Builder "Bob the Builder")_, _[Cars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cars\_(franchise) "Cars (franchise)")_, _[Dora the Explorer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dora\_the\_Explorer\_(TV\_series) "Dora the Explorer (TV series)")_, _[Hana's Helpline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hana's\_Helpline "Hana's Helpline")_, _[Ben and Holly's Little Kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben\_and\_Holly's\_Little\_Kingdom "Ben and Holly's Little Kingdom")_, _[Sooty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sooty "Sooty")_ and _[Teletubbies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teletubbies "Teletubbies")_.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Bear_Toys#cite_note-4) They also produce new properties, like Bush Baby World.

"My First Thomas & Friends" is a range of chunky plastic toys. The range started in c.1994, and was advertised for young infants who enjoyed the series. The models were safe for younger fans to play with, and included most of the major and minor characters from the TV Series.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Bear_Toys#cite_note-5)

The company also acquired the rights to sell the [London 2012 Olympic and Paralympic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics "2012 Summer Olympics") mascots [Wenlock and Mandeville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wenlock_and_Mandeville "Wenlock and Mandeville").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Bear_Toys#cite_note-:0-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Bear_Toys#cite_note-:1-2) In 2012 the company also launched a range of pre-school vehicles under the brand name Go MINI which was officially licensed by BMW MINI. They also launched a range of Something Special toys featuring the popular BBC character Mr Tumble.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Bear_Toys#cite_note-6)

**Waddingtons** was a British manufacturer of [card](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Card_games "Card games") and [board games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Board_games "Board games"). The company was founded by John Waddington of [Leeds, England](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leeds,_England "Leeds, England") and the manager, actor and playwright [Wilson Barrett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilson_Barrett "Wilson Barrett"), under the name _Waddingtons Limited_. The name was changed in 1905 to _John Waddington Limited_, then _Waddington's House of Games_, then _Waddington Games_, and finally just _Waddingtons_.

## Founding and history

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Waddingtons&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Founding and history")]

The company was established as a printing business, and at first 'practically all its business related to the theatre'.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waddingtons#cite_note-1) It entered into game production in 1922, due to a boom in demand for playing cards around [World War I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_I "World War I").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waddingtons#cite_note-TTT-2) Waddingtons subsequently sold both original games (especially tie-ins for UK television programmes) and games licensed from other publishers.

Waddingtons became the UK publisher of the US [Parker Brothers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parker_Brothers "Parker Brothers")' [Monopoly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monopoly_(game) "Monopoly (game)"), while Parker licensed Waddingtons' [Cluedo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cluedo "Cluedo").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waddingtons#cite_note-TTT-2) In 1941, the British [Directorate of Military Intelligence section 9](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MI9 "MI9") (MI9) had the company create a special edition of Monopoly for [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II")[prisoners of war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prisoner_of_war "Prisoner of war") held by the Germans.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waddingtons#cite_note-3) Hidden inside these games were maps, compasses, real money and other objects useful for escaping. They were distributed to prisoners by fake charitable organisations.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waddingtons#cite_note-4) In 2024, an immersive, life-sized monopoly was created in Leeds in honor of Waddingtons.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waddingtons#cite_note-5)

In the years 1971 to 1985 the firm printed 13 different sets of postage stamps for the Hong Kong Post Office.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waddingtons#cite_note-6)

[Victor Watson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Watson "Victor Watson"), the grandson of Victor Hugo Watson was its chairman from 1977 to 1993.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waddingtons#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waddingtons#cite_note-8) While well known for games, they never provided more than 15% of profit; Victor continued his father Norman's emphasis on improving packaging technology, such as folding cartons and microwave trays. From the 1970s, the popularity of [video games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Video_game "Video game") hurt game sales, and after Victor's retirement,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waddingtons#cite_note-9) the company was bought by [Hasbro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hasbro "Hasbro") in 1994.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waddingtons#cite_note-10)

Beginning in 1994, [Christmas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christmas "Christmas")-themed [jigsaw puzzles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jigsaw_puzzles "Jigsaw puzzles") were released annually until 2007. The first twelve in the series depicted a scene from a [Victorian-era](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victorian_era "Victorian era") Christmas. The final puzzle depicted a scene from the [fairy tale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fairy_tale "Fairy tale")[Cinderella](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinderella "Cinderella"). The small number of puzzles, combined with them being limited editions, has made these puzzles highly collectable. Further jigsaws have been produced since 2010 by a new company, using the same brand name.

**Companies that won a BATR Toy Award in 1997/98 and are no longer independent entities (i.e., closed or bought and now operating under a different name) – as of 2020**

| Award (1997/98) | Winning company | Current status (≤ 2020) | How it is “no longer in business” or “under a different name” |
|-----------------|-----------------|-------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------|
| **BATR Toy of the Year** – *Teletubbies* | **Golden Bear Products Ltd.** | *Still active* – the brand continues to operate under the same name. | – |
| **Most Innovative Toy** – *Tamagotchi* | **Bandai** | *Still active* – Bandai remains a major toy manufacturer worldwide. | – |
| **Game of the Year** – *Star Wars Monopoly* | **Waddingtons Ltd.** | **Acquired by Hasbro in 1994**; the original company was dissolved and its brands (Monopoly, Cluedo, etc.) are now licensed and manufactured under the Hasbro umbrella. | Waddingtons is no longer an independent business; its brand assets are now part of Hasbro. |
| **Boys Toy of the Year** – *Action Man Skydiver* | **Hasbro** | *Still active* – Hasbro continues to operate as a global toy conglomerate. | – |
| **Girls Toy of the Year** – *Baby Expressions* | **Famosa (Spain)** | *Status unclear* – no reliable recent evidence that Famosa still operates as an independent Spanish toy house; most references point to a short‑lived line. | If it is no longer active, it would be considered closed; if it is still trading under a different corporate structure (e.g., part of a larger Spanish toy group), it would be under a different name. |
| **Toy Company of the Year** – *Toy Options Ltd.* | **Toy Options Ltd.** | *Little publicly available information; the company appears to have gone out of business or been absorbed into a larger supplier later in the 2000s.* | Zero public evidence of continued independent operations up to 2020; likely dissolved or merged. |
| **Other Nominees** (Nano Pals – Playmates, etc.) | **Playmates Toys Ltd.,** **Lego,** **Presents** | *Still active* – all remain operating under their original brands. | – |

### Summary
Only **Waddingtons** is a clear case of a 1997‑98 BATR award‑winning company that **no longer exists as an independent entity**: it was bought by Hasbro in 1994 and its original corporate identity was dissolved. All other award‑winning companies (Golden Bear, Bandai, Hasbro, Toy Options, Famosa) either remain in business or lack definitive evidence of closure/non‑existence (Toy Options and Famosa). Therefore, **Waddingtons** is the single company that fits the criteria of “not in business before 2020, or purchased and now under a different name.”
